content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've searched the forum but couldn't find an answer to my question. Is there a way to display and use decimal numbers (such as 0.05, 0.5, 0.005, etc.) on [product_name] [version_no]?

The analog values in [product_name] only work with INTEGER format, meaning only fixed-point numbers are possible and floating point operations are not available. The supported value range is -32768 to 32767. The display of [product_name] or [product_name] [product_name] can be set to show up to 3 decimal places: Without decimals: -32768 to 32767; One decimal: -3276.8 to 3276.7; Two decimals: -327.68 to 327.67; Three decimals: -32.768 to 32.767.
Very helpful, thank you. What is the purpose of the "Float/Integer Converter" and "Integer/Float Converter" function blocks?
Those blocks are intended for MODBUS values, as MODBUS supports floating point numbers.

Where is the MODBUS port on [product_name] [version_no] FS4? There is only one port and it's an Ethernet port (RJ45). How do I physically connect a [product_name] FS4, for example, to a [product_name] panel via MODBUS? I'm asking about the hardware connection. Thank you for any guidance.

[product_name] FS04 supports MODBUS TCP/IP but not RTU. The MODBUS port is the same as the Ethernet port, as there is only one port. I'm not sure if a [product_name] panel supports MODBUS. It's important to note that [product_name] supports only fixed-point numbers, so the value range is limited to -32768 to 32767.

Hi, To connect an HMI to [product_name], it's better to use the default protocol rather than MODBUS. This is available with any HMI starting from [version_no]. Advantages include simpler configuration and access to more addresses. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are exploring how to work with decimal numbers in [product_name] [version_no], and learn that only integer (fixed-point) formats are natively handled with customizable decimal display up to three digits. There is confusion about the function of float/integer converter blocks, mainly concerning MODBUS communication. The thread also discusses practical challenges regarding how to connect devices via MODBUS and the differences between fixed-point and floating-point support.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that [product_name] [version_no] will support decimal numbers directly, offer clear float/integer conversion options, and provide straightforward methods for hardware connectivity to HMI panels, preferably via MODBUS or default protocols.
